standard_prerequisites.name: Differential graded algebras and bimodules
standard_prerequisites.statement: Dg R-algebras (A,d), (B,d), a dg (A,B)-bimodule N, and the opposite algebra A^opp.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the setting of the statement (source lines 5611-5614).

standard_prerequisites.name: Property (P)
standard_prerequisites.statement: The class of dg modules with property (P) used to construct the derived tensor product, closed under the identifications of a bimodule with a left and a right module structure.
standard_prerequisites.use: The hypothesis on N and the reason the ordinary tensor product computes the derived one (source lines 5613-5614, 5626-5628).

standard_prerequisites.name: Construction of the derived tensor product
standard_prerequisites.statement: The construction of - tensor^L_A N from a resolution by property-(P) objects of the first variable (the author's lemma-derived-bc, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what turns the quasi-isomorphism claim into the stated computation (source lines 5622-5623).

standard_prerequisites.name: Functoriality of the tensor product under quasi-isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.statement: If one of the variables of the tensor product is replaced by a quasi-isomorphic dg module with property (P), the tensor product map is a quasi-isomorphism (the author's lemma-functoriality-bc, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the last step of the proof (source lines 5628-5629).

core_obligations: Reduce to a statement about quasi-isomorphisms: show that for a quasi-isomorphism f : M to M' of dg A-modules the induced map f tensor id on M tensor_A N to M' tensor_A N is again a quasi-isomorphism (source lines 5619-5622).
Connect that reduction to the derived functor: use the construction of the derived tensor product to conclude the computation (source lines 5622-5623).

Change sides: observe that the map only depends on the left A-module structure of N, identify M tensor_A N with N tensor_{A^opp} M, and use that N has property (P) as a dg A^opp-module (source lines 5624-5628).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to the quasi-isomorphism invariance of tensoring with N in the first variable.
Use the construction of the derived tensor product to pass from that invariance to the computation of M tensor^L_A N.
Rewrite the tensor product as a tensor product over the opposite algebra and use property (P) on that side.
Invoke the functoriality lemma and conclude.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-compute-bc at source lines 5609-5616: for dg R-algebras (A,d), (B,d) and a dg (A,B)-bimodule N with property (P) as a left dg A-module, the derived tensor product M tensor^L_A N is computed by the ordinary tensor product M tensor_A N for every dg A-module M. The proof at source lines 5618-5630 reduces the claim to the invariance of the ordinary tensor product under a quasi-isomorphism in the first variable, which depends only on the left A-module structure of N, and then identifies M tensor_A N with N tensor_{A^opp} M and applies the functoriality lemma, using that N also has property (P) as a dg A^opp-module. It is short, and its substance is seeing which variable may be replaced, and why the property-(P) hypothesis has to be read for the opposite algebra.
